{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
    "line": 51,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "concurrency",
    "title": "Async legacy writes inherit request context and are canceled",
    "body": "In Create (and the same pattern in Delete at line 110, Update at line 135, and DeleteCollection at line 163), the goroutine derives context.WithTimeoutCause from the incoming ctx. In the apiserver this ctx is the request context, which is canceled as soon as the handler returns. Since these legacy writes are scheduled asynchronously after the unified-store write and after the handler returns, they generally start with an already canceled context and are aborted before writing. Mode 3 reads only from unified storage, so legacy is the safety copy; missed legacy creates/updates/deletes can mean lost safety data. Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a fresh background context before adding the timeout."
  },
  {
    "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
    "line": 106,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "perf",
    "title": "Delete records object name in metric kind label",
    "body": "After a successful Storage.Delete, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage). Every other call passes options.Kind as the third argument. Using the deleted object name as the kind label creates an unbounded Prometheus series per object name, causing high cardinality on delete operations and making the metric impossible to aggregate by resource kind. Pass options.Kind instead of name."
  },
  {
    "file": "pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go",
    "line": 523,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "test_gap",
    "title": "Mode3 integration test asserts immediate legacy consistency after async writes",
    "body": "The new mode3 cases run doPlaylistTests, where k8s create/update/delete now propagate to legacy asynchronously. The test immediately queries the legacy /api/playlists endpoint at line 523 and uses getFromBothAPIs around lines 535 and 547 without waiting or polling for the async legacy write to finish. This makes the mode3 integration tests racy: they can fail when the goroutine has not completed, or pass while the legacy safety write is actually broken. The test should poll or otherwise await eventual convergence before asserting legacy state."
  },
  {
    "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
    "line": 139,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "Legacy update reuses the same UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the unified-storage result",
    "body": "Update passes the same objInfo to both d.Storage.Update and, asynchronously, d.Legacy.Update. UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject is invoked independently by each store against its own old object; it is not guaranteed to be idempotent or to produce the same object when legacy is stale. The previous implementation wrapped the object returned from unified storage before sending it to legacy, which ensured both stores wrote the same updated object. Without that, legacy may store a different version from unified storage, defeating the safety copy and potentially causing legacy update failures."
  },
  {
    "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
    "line": 55,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "Async legacy Create uses original obj rather than the object returned by Storage",
    "body": "Create passes the original request obj to d.Legacy.Create instead of the created object returned by d.Storage.Create. If unified storage assigns server-generated fields such as a generated name, UID, or resourceVersion only on the returned object without mutating obj, the legacy write will generate or record a different identity than unified storage. That leaves mode3 with two divergent objects for the same logical create. The legacy writer should receive the object identity returned by unified storage."
  },
  {
    "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
    "line": 45,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Storage create/update failures are recorded as legacy duration",
    "body": "On a failed Storage.Create, line 45 calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), and the same occurs for Storage.Update at line 129. No legacy operation was attempted in these paths, and startStorage measures the unified-store call. This records storage failures and latency in the legacy metric while leaving the storage metric missing those failures. These paths should call recordStorageDuration, and recordLegacyDuration should be used only after actual Legacy calls."
  },
  {
    "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
    "line": 166,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "DeleteCollection records legacy duration in the storage metric",
    "body": "In the DeleteCollection goroutine, after d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). This records the legacy operation as a storage operation, corrupting both storage and legacy latency/error metrics and hiding failures in the legacy safety write. It should call d.recordLegacyDuration."
  },
  {
    "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go",
    "line": 65,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "test_gap",
    "title": "Mode3 unit tests do not wait for or assert legacy writes",
    "body": "The Mode3 Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection tests launch asynchronous legacy writes but do not wait for the goroutines and do not assert that Legacy.Create, Legacy.Update, Legacy.Delete, or Legacy.DeleteCollection were called. An implementation could skip the legacy write entirely and these tests would still pass, and the current context-cancellation issue would not be detected. Add a wait mechanism and assertions for the expected legacy calls."
  }
]}

findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit request context and are canceled
findings.body: In Create (and the same pattern in Delete at line 110, Update at line 135, and DeleteCollection at line 163), the goroutine derives context.WithTimeoutCause from the incoming ctx. In the apiserver this ctx is the request context, which is canceled as soon as the handler returns. Since these legacy writes are scheduled asynchronously after the unified-store write and after the handler returns, they generally start with an already canceled context and are aborted before writing. Mode 3 reads only from unified storage, so legacy is the safety copy; missed legacy creates/updates/deletes can mean lost safety data. Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a fresh background context before adding the timeout.

findings.title: Delete records object name in metric kind label
findings.body: After a successful Storage.Delete, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage). Every other call passes options.Kind as the third argument. Using the deleted object name as the kind label creates an unbounded Prometheus series per object name, causing high cardinality on delete operations and making the metric impossible to aggregate by resource kind. Pass options.Kind instead of name.

findings.title: Mode3 integration test asserts immediate legacy consistency after async writes
findings.body: The new mode3 cases run doPlaylistTests, where k8s create/update/delete now propagate to legacy asynchronously. The test immediately queries the legacy /api/playlists endpoint at line 523 and uses getFromBothAPIs around lines 535 and 547 without waiting or polling for the async legacy write to finish. This makes the mode3 integration tests racy: they can fail when the goroutine has not completed, or pass while the legacy safety write is actually broken. The test should poll or otherwise await eventual convergence before asserting legacy state.

findings.title: Legacy update reuses the same UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the unified-storage result
findings.body: Update passes the same objInfo to both d.Storage.Update and, asynchronously, d.Legacy.Update. UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject is invoked independently by each store against its own old object; it is not guaranteed to be idempotent or to produce the same object when legacy is stale. The previous implementation wrapped the object returned from unified storage before sending it to legacy, which ensured both stores wrote the same updated object. Without that, legacy may store a different version from unified storage, defeating the safety copy and potentially causing legacy update failures.

findings.title: Async legacy Create uses original obj rather than the object returned by Storage
findings.body: Create passes the original request obj to d.Legacy.Create instead of the created object returned by d.Storage.Create. If unified storage assigns server-generated fields such as a generated name, UID, or resourceVersion only on the returned object without mutating obj, the legacy write will generate or record a different identity than unified storage. That leaves mode3 with two divergent objects for the same logical create. The legacy writer should receive the object identity returned by unified storage.

findings.title: Storage create/update failures are recorded as legacy duration
findings.body: On a failed Storage.Create, line 45 calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), and the same occurs for Storage.Update at line 129. No legacy operation was attempted in these paths, and startStorage measures the unified-store call. This records storage failures and latency in the legacy metric while leaving the storage metric missing those failures. These paths should call recordStorageDuration, and recordLegacyDuration should be used only after actual Legacy calls.

findings.title: DeleteCollection records legacy duration in the storage metric
findings.body: In the DeleteCollection goroutine, after d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). This records the legacy operation as a storage operation, corrupting both storage and legacy latency/error metrics and hiding failures in the legacy safety write. It should call d.recordLegacyDuration.

findings.title: Mode3 unit tests do not wait for or assert legacy writes
findings.body: The Mode3 Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection tests launch asynchronous legacy writes but do not wait for the goroutines and do not assert that Legacy.Create, Legacy.Update, Legacy.Delete, or Legacy.DeleteCollection were called. An implementation could skip the legacy write entirely and these tests would still pass, and the current context-cancellation issue would not be detected. Add a wait mechanism and assertions for the expected legacy calls.
